chapter: Porgy and Bess and Varsity Show
title: Buck as Bingo and being a vaudevillian in opera
summary: Buck played an insignificant part, but Bubbles insisted he come along; he says his vaudeville background fitted Sportin' Life.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: He was Bingo, that's just an insignificant part, you know.
Were you both billed as headliners?
No -- no, no, just billed as a character of the show. There was no Buck and Bubbles -- it was billed to John Bubbles, understand?
That was one of the things that you insisted upon thought with the show that Buck went with you?

That's right. That's exactly it. They wanted me without Buck. I said no, because Buck was a character that stood out. Gershwin picked me because I was able to move around and act like a person of the Sportin' Life class, you know. He didn't do a bad pick, 'cause I don't know anybody else

in my race could have did that part any better. 'Cause there ain't nobody gifted to that extent. Don't forget I was a vaudevillian, going into opera. See the point? Which was more helpful for me than the average person, just pick up and do the part. All the Sportin' Lifes they're getting now just can sing and are put in there. It's a difficult part to go around and do the part I had to do.
